inspection_boundary: Only inspected preserved real Android bytecode, not invoked Robolectric/shadow behavior.
observed_runtime_failure: The second device diagnostic reached Os.stat of an enumerated /proc/self/fd entry and received EACCES. That failure is retained; descriptor lifetime verification did not pass.
proposed_algorithm: Snapshot every own /proc/self/fd numeric filename before creating a probe-owned descriptor. Failure to enumerate or parse must fail, not return zero.

For each snapshotted original descriptor number call real ParcelFileDescriptor.fromFd(number). The inspected Android 15 implementation duplicates it using Os.fcntlInt(F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC) on Q+ or F_DUPFD otherwise; it never adopts/detaches or closes the caller descriptor.

Catch only IOException whose cause is ErrnoException with EBADF from fromFd/native duplication (concurrently closed original). Rethrow any other duplication exception; fstat and close failures remain failures.
Within duplicate.use, call real Os.fstat(duplicate.fileDescriptor), compare actual st_dev/st_ino, and close that duplicate before advancing to the next original number.
Do not read, write or seek on probe-owned duplicates. fstat inspects metadata and does not change the shared open-file-description offset.
Keep existing positive known-open file descriptor assertions and post-close zero assertions. Do not broad-suppress EACCES or filter away hardlink/deleted/pipe identities.
proposed_positive_control: In a separately authorized additive device helper self-test, open one task-owned file handle, position it via Os.lseek, run repeated probe counts, and assert exactly one matching identity and unchanged real offset. Close the handle and assert zero.

Create an actual ParcelFileDescriptor pipe, record identity via Os.fstat, assert two matching ends; close one and assert one; close both and assert zero. Repeated scans must not accumulate dup handles.
Run the actual existing FileProvider source-through-EOF test and reliable-pipe-error tests; all production read/close counters and byte assertions remain mandatory.
limits: Static bytecode does not prove the emulator SELinux policy allows fstat or that duplication succeeds; only the rerun can establish that.
Enumeration and scanning are not an atomic process-wide descriptor census; documented tests concern task-owned identities after controlled operations.
No overall app memory, FD dump, other-process introspection, file-offset mutation, hidden/reflection or root-only device access is proposed.
